title: Crash, restart, late writes and cancel: the accepted prefix is preserved and unfinished work is replayable
annotator: claude-sonnet-5.5 worker (a language model), annotation on 2026-10-24 from the written blueprint; no program produced any expected value; the owner has not signed off
independence_statement: Each case is a short story with a chosen frozen workset, an event timeline and written outcomes. The outcomes follow the written blueprint rules: one accepted terminal per frozen occurrence, claim-fenced atomic acceptance, accepted-key reuse on replay, bridge-closed cancel with drain, and a pending workset until the finalizer commits. No msgloom store, finalizer, runner or A2 code was run or imported. The reference checker in the test file only validates the written answers.

sources: A2 Kedro v2 architecture blueprint of 2026-10-23, section 4.2: every ordered frozen occurrence needs exactly one persisted accepted terminal; the deduplicated selection refs are not enough; COMPLETE only when everything is accepted and complete; any limitation gives terminal INCOMPLETE

same blueprint, section 4.3: the versioned finalizer re-checks the PREPARE claim and every accepted result; a failed step rolls back and the workset stays pending; a missing ref or an invalid claim cannot become a success

same blueprint, section 5.1: the logical key is deterministic and includes the frozen configuration version; the key does not include time, attempt or output digest; replay finds the key and returns the stored result; the original record stays unchanged

same blueprint, section 5.3: append_or_verify_a2_stage requires the live claim first, then reuses an accepted key or inserts one atomic record; an accepted prefix written by earlier attempts is reusable; post-COMMIT cancel is not a rollback; the next run skips accepted stages and does not rerun the parser
same blueprint, section 6.1: one owner runner worker per workset; on cancel the bridge-closed flag is set, later nodes and new saves are rejected, then in-flight work drains

same blueprint, section 8.2: outcome table (claim lost gives FAILED scheduled-claim-lost; user cancel gives CANCELLED scheduled-cancelled; trusted partial gives INCOMPLETE scheduled-preparation-incomplete)
A2 Kedro v2 execution plan of 2026-10-23, task T0-07: crash, restart, late writes and cancel; the accepted prefix is saved and unfinished work must be replayable

same blueprint, section 4.3 steps 3 to 6: the terminal update is one transaction; a v2 finalizer that meets an already terminal row must reject; old terminal history is immutable; duplicate finalization is a required negative test

PROPOSED POLICY (T0-07-P10 and T0-07-N07 only): the blueprint does not say whether an operator replay may run under a changed configuration (P10), or what a save by the live claim does after the workset is terminal (N07). See the case rationale.
TASK GOAL (T0-07-P05 only): the task goal says cancel drains pending writes. See the case rationale.

model.ops: claim = a process takes the live claim token for a configuration (first run, restart or takeover; it replaces the previous live token); crash = the process dies, uncommitted work is lost; cancel = the bridge-closed flag is set; write = one occurrence result is saved with the named claim token; finalize = the finalizer tries to move the workset from pending to terminal
model.write_outcomes: accepted = new atomic accepted record; reused = the key was already accepted, the stored id is returned and the parser does not run; rejected_stale_claim = the token is not the live token, checked before anything else, also after the workset is terminal; rejected_already_terminal (oracle label) = the live token writes after the workset is terminal (PROPOSED, T0-07-N07); rejected_bridge_closed = a new save after cancel; rolled_back = the transaction did not reach COMMIT, nothing is stored
model.finalize_outcomes: terminal_complete, terminal_incomplete, rejected_stale_claim, rejected_missing_accepted (some frozen occurrence has no accepted result; the workset stays pending), rejected_already_terminal (oracle label; the row is already terminal, blueprint 4.3 step 4; the terminal row does not change)
model.accepted_prefix: the frozen occurrences are processed in order by one owner worker, so the accepted set of one configuration is always the first k occurrences
model.result_ids: res-<config>-<ordinal> are chosen placeholders for the deterministic accepted result of that configuration and occurrence
model.snapshot: state after the named event; accepted lists the accepted occurrence ordinals per configuration; replayable is frozen minus accepted for the active configuration

cases.title: Crash before the first accept: nothing is accepted and all three occurrences are replayable
Crash in the middle of a batch: the first three results survive and replay reuses their ids
Write interrupted before COMMIT: nothing is stored and that occurrence is replayable
Crash after the last accept but before the finalizer: all results survive, the workset is still pending, restart only finalizes
cases.rationale: Without a committed finalizer the workset row is still pending (blueprint 4.3). Replay finds every accepted key, so no parser runs and no id changes (blueprint 5.3).

cases.title: Cancel while a write is in flight: the in-flight write drains whole, a later save is refused
cases.rationale: TASK GOAL decision. Blueprint 6.1 says the bridge-closed flag rejects new saves and in-flight work drains. It does not say that a draining save must commit. The task goal says cancel drains pending writes and leaves no half result. The oracle reads this as: a draining save finishes its own atomic transaction and is then fully accepted. P05 shows the committed case. N02 shows the rolled-back case. A crash event ends the cancelled process before claim-B starts, so this case needs no takeover without a crash.

cases.title: Cancel after COMMIT: the caller saw a cancel, the data is accepted, and the next run reuses it
cases.rationale: Blueprint 5.3: post-COMMIT cancel is not a rollback. The next run reads by key and skips the accepted stage. The parser does not run again. A crash event ends the cancelled process before claim-B starts.

cases.title: Double restart: every restart sees the same prefix and the same ids, and only the missing tail is written
An accepted result with a limitation is accepted, not replayable; the workset ends terminal INCOMPLETE
cases.rationale: Blueprint 4.2: prepared@2 with an explicit limitation is a valid accepted terminal. Any limitation gives terminal INCOMPLETE. The limited occurrence is not replayed and not pending.

cases.title: Two occurrences share one source ref: the accepted result of the first never satisfies the second
cases.rationale: Blueprint 4.2: each ordered frozen occurrence needs its own accepted terminal. The deduplicated source refs are not enough. The logical key includes the partition ordinal, so occurrence 2 gets its own result id.

cases.title: PROPOSED POLICY: operator replay under a changed configuration creates a new key and new ids; the old accepted records stay unchanged
cases.rationale: PROPOSED POLICY requiring owner sign-off. Blueprint 5.1 puts the frozen configuration version in the logical key, so a different configuration gives different keys and different ids. Blueprint 5.1 and 5.3 keep an accepted record unchanged. In this case the workset is still pending when claim-B starts with cfg-2. Blueprint 4.3 step 5 covers an operator replay of a terminal workset: it appends a new attempt and receipt and does not overwrite the terminal row. It does not cover this pending case. The blueprint does not say that a workset frozen under cfg-1 may be replayed under cfg-2, who may approve it, or how the terminal receipt names the configuration. The oracle proposes: the replay is allowed, the cfg-1 records stay, and the cfg-2 records are new.

cases.title: Late writes and a late finalize from a lost claim are rejected, even for an occurrence that is already accepted
cases.rationale: Blueprint 5.3 checks the live claim before it looks up the accepted key, so a stale writer cannot even reuse. Blueprint 4.3 re-checks the PREPARE claim in the finalizer. Blueprint 8.2 maps a lost claim to FAILED scheduled-claim-lost and blocks new saves. This case has a takeover without a crash. Blueprint 6.1 says the lease has no automatic renewal, so a slow worker can outlive its lease. Blueprint 8.2 treats a lost or invalid live claim as a normal condition. The blueprint does not say how claim-B is granted while claim-A still runs. The oracle does not model that step.

cases.title: Cancel with an in-flight write that does not reach COMMIT: no half result, later saves refused, the tail stays replayable
cases.rationale: A save is one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction (blueprint 5.3). It is accepted whole or not at all. The occurrence that was in flight has no result after the rollback and is replayable. A crash event ends the cancelled process before claim-B starts.

cases.title: The finalizer refuses to finish while a frozen occurrence has no accepted result; the workset stays pending
cases.rationale: Blueprint 4.2 and 4.3: every ordered frozen occurrence needs an accepted terminal, the finalizer verifies each one, a missing ref cannot become a success, and a failed step rolls back to pending.

cases.title: Duplicate finalize on a terminal COMPLETE workset is rejected, from the same claim and from a restarted claim; the terminal snapshot does not change
cases.rationale: Blueprint 4.3 step 4: a v2 finalizer that meets an already terminal row must reject. Step 5: old terminal history is immutable. Step 6 lists duplicate finalization as a required negative test. The second finalize is rejected, whether it comes from the same claim or from a later claim. The terminal snapshot does not change. The blueprint names the rejection but gives no error code. The name rejected_already_terminal is an oracle label.

cases.title: Duplicate finalize on a terminal INCOMPLETE workset is rejected; it does not turn INCOMPLETE into COMPLETE
cases.rationale: Blueprint 4.2: any limitation gives terminal INCOMPLETE. Blueprint 4.3 step 4 and step 5: a finalizer that meets an already terminal row must reject, and old terminal history is immutable. The second finalize does not remove the limitation and does not give COMPLETE. The terminal snapshot does not change.

cases.title: Late write from a superseded claim after the workset is terminal is rejected, even for an occurrence that is already accepted; the terminal snapshot does not change
cases.rationale: Blueprint 5.3 makes the live-claim check the first step of every save, before the accepted-key lookup. A writer with a superseded token is rejected even when the workset is already terminal (see also N01). Blueprint 4.3 step 5: old terminal history is immutable, so the terminal snapshot does not change. The blueprint does not say whether a stale finalize on a terminal row reports a stale claim or an already terminal row. The oracle does not model that order. The checker rejects such a timeline.

cases.title: PROPOSED POLICY: a write by the live claim after its own workset is terminal is rejected; the terminal snapshot does not change
cases.rationale: PROPOSED POLICY requiring owner sign-off. Blueprint 4.3 step 4 rejects a second finalize on a terminal row, and step 5 keeps terminal history immutable. The blueprint does not say what a save does when the live claim holder writes after its own workset became terminal. It does not say whether the claim stays live after the terminal update. It does not say whether the save returns the stored result (the blueprint 5.3 reuse path) or is rejected. The oracle proposes rejected_already_terminal, no result id and no change to the terminal snapshot. The alternative is reused with the stored id.
